title: SIG questionnaire walkthrough - Verdant Insurance
next_steps: Jordan Lee: Send SOC 2 Type II report and compliance pack link by 2026-03-30
Ava Chen: Share architecture diagram (encryption/KMS + VPC setup) and RBAC screenshots by 2026-03-31
Verdant (Marta): Return filled SIG matrix with priority evidence items by 2026-04-06
Schedule follow-up technical deep dive / demo for Verdant infra team week of 2026-04-06
action_items: Jordan Lee: Provide SOC 2 Type II PDF and bridge letter if available - due 2026-03-30
Ava Chen: Export RBAC screenshots, SAML/SCIM config example, and key management diagram - due 2026-03-31
Riley Patel: Pull recent pen test summary and incident response playbook excerpt - due 2026-04-02
Marta Gomez: Identify any EU data residency proof required and mark highest priority SIG questions - due 2026-04-06
summary: Walkthrough of Verdant Insurance SIG questions focusing on SOC 2/ISO posture, RBAC/SSO provisioning, audit logs and retention, data residency (EU), and encryption/KMS options. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 Type II, architecture diagram, RBAC screenshots; Verdant to prioritize SIG items and return matrix. Follow-up technical deep dive scheduled week of 2026-04-06.
topics: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 status
Encryption at rest/in transit, KMS, BYOK
transcript: [00:00] Jordan Lee: Hi everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Jordan, AE on the account. Ava is our solutions engineer and Riley is on security. Quick confirm on attendees?
[00:12] Marta Gomez: Hi Jordan, this is Marta, vendor risk. Also have Liam (CISO) and Dinah from infra on. We want to go line-by-line on the SIG and call out where we need evidence.

[00:25] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Goal 60	60 minute walkthrough, surface any gaps and commit to evidence and owners. We'll try to keep to the high priority items first: SOC 2, encryption/KMS, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, data residency.

[00:43] Ava Chen: Quick note, some of the answers will differ if you're evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. For Verdant, you mentioned EU data residency	6 we'll focus on our EU region options and private VPC controls.
[01:02] Liam O'Connor: Correct. We need assurance that EU data stays in-region and that keys can be customer-managed. Also interested in RBAC and SCIM provisioning with Okta.

[01:18] Riley Patel: On SOC 2, we are Type II through 2025-11 and our report covers logical access, change management, and availability controls. We'll share the report; redactions for customer PII are standard.
[01:35] Marta Gomez: Great	6 when you share, we need the cover letter and description of scope. Also do you have ISO 27001 cert in progress?
[01:46] Jordan Lee: We're mapped to ISO controls and have an internal program, but formal ISO 27001 certification is in progress	6 not yet certified. We'll state that clearly in the evidence pack.
[02:02] Dinah Park: Can you detail how RBAC works? We need to see admin separation, least privilege, and an audit trail of permission changes.

[02:12] Ava Chen: Sure. We support role-based roles scoped per-organization and per-route. SCIM provisioning + SAML for SSO (Okta, Azure AD). We can provide screenshots of the Roles page and an export of role assignments. Note: the UI name is sometimes Redwood Console in the transcript	6 occasionally transcribed as 'Redwood consol' or 'Redwood con sol'.
[02:34] Marta Gomez: Haha, the transcript is already foreshadowing. On SAML, do you support signed assertions and IdP-initiated?

[02:41] Riley Patel: Yes, signed assertions and both IdP/SP initiated flows. SCIM supports group sync and deprovisioning. We keep an audit log of SSO provisioning events that we can surface as evidence.
[03:00] Liam O'Connor: What about encryption? At-rest, in-transit, and key management	6 can we BYOK and integrate with our KMS/HSM?

[03:10] Ava Chen: Encryption in transit is TLS 1.2/1.3. At-rest we use AES-256. For Hosted we offer customer-managed keys via AWS KMS in supported regions	6 BYOK for Dedicated/Private is supported with HSM integrations. We'll share an architecture diagram showing where keys live and the option for customer KMS.
[03:34] Marta Gomez: Are keys ever accessible by Redwood staff?

[03:38] Riley Patel: For customer-managed KMS keys, Redwood does not have direct access to key material. For platform-managed keys we manage rotation but access is limited to a small ops group with multi-factor controls; we'll include key custody policy excerpt in the evidence.
[03:55] Dinah Park: How long are audit logs retained? We require at least one year, ideally two for some regs.

[04:01] Ava Chen: Default retention is 13 months for audit logs in Hosted; for Dedicated we can configure longer retention and export to customer buckets (S3) or SIEMs. We'll note the retention policy and export options.
[04:18] Jordan Lee: Also want to call out tracing and per-token/route logs are available for debugging; PII is redacted by default but we can show the redaction policy and sample logs.
[04:32] Marta Gomez: Data residency: we need to ensure data in EU stays in EU for both storage and processing. Does Redwood do any cross-region processing for model tuning or telemetry?

[04:45] Riley Patel: No cross-region processing without customer opt-in. For Hosted we route EU customers to EU regions; Dedicated/Private stay in-customer VPC or region. Telemetry for platform health is aggregated but can be configured to exclude payloads; we can provide the telemetry policy.
[05:05] Liam O'Connor: About model variants	6 you mentioned fallback to compatible models. If a fallback happens, could data cross regions?

[05:12] Ava Chen: Our smart routing respects region policy; fallbacks are to models in the same region or to pre-approved variants. If you opt into cross-region fallback that's a config we would document	6 but default is region-bound.
[05:28] Marta Gomez: For the SIG, they ask for penetration test results and vuln management. Do you have recent pen test summary or 3rd party scans?

[05:36] Riley Patel: We have a third-party annual pen test; we'll share a redacted summary and our remediation timeline. We also run weekly internal scans and have a patching SLA that we'll include in the evidence list.
[05:52] Dinah Park: Logging integrations	6 can we forward logs to our Splunk/Datadog?

[05:57] Ava Chen: Yes, log forwarding via secure export (TLS) to customer endpoints is supported; for Dedicated we often set up direct VPC peering and logging exports to S3, then you can pick up with your SIEM.

[06:10] Jordan Lee: Quick interjection	6 typical evidence we provide for SIG: SOC 2 Type II report, pen test summary, architecture diagram, network diagram, RBAC screenshots, SAML config sample, KMS integration doc, data processing agreement. We'll map these to SIG question IDs.
[06:26] Marta Gomez: That's helpful. For the SIG matrix there's a handful of high-impact Qs: cryptography, key custody, access control, incident response. We'll flag those as priority.

[06:40] Ava Chen: We'll put together a prioritized evidence bundle. Also, a note: some SIG/CAIQ questions ask for very specific control names	6 where our wording differs we provide a control mapping doc to translate platform features to SIG control language.
[06:56] Liam O'Connor: On incident response: SLA on incident notification and post-incident reports?

[07:02] Riley Patel: Our standard incident notification is within 72 hours for high severity, with a post-incident report within 10 business days; for enterprise customers we can contract shorter windows. We'll include the IR playbook excerpt and escalation matrix.
[07:22] Marta Gomez: Can you walk through a few SIG questions live? For example, cryptographic key lifecycle (Q4.2-ish).

[07:30] Ava Chen: Sure, reading from our mapping	6 keys are generated in KMS, rotated per policy (90	6365 days depending on key type), retirement processes documented, and destruction logs retained. For BYOK we require KMS policies that prevent key export.
[07:48] Dinah Park: Is there KMS rotation automation? If customer manages keys, how is rotation coordinated?

[07:54] Riley Patel: If customer manages keys in their KMS, they control rotation. We support key rotation events and will accept new key versions; we provide an operational runbook for rotation steps to avoid downtime.

[08:08] Jordan Lee: Small transcribe note	6 sometimes product names like "KV cache" come through in the SIG but that's more implementation detail; customers rarely need the KV cache specifics, mostly access and encryption controls.
[08:20] Marta Gomez: For audit evidence, can you provide an export of audit logs showing role changes and SSO events?
[08:27] Ava Chen: Yes, we can provide a redacted export showing role assignment change events for a sample period. We'll annotate the export to show the mapping between event fields and SIG controls.
[08:41] Liam O'Connor: Regarding SLAs and uptime, do you have an enterprise SLA? We need availability numbers and credits.

[08:48] Jordan Lee: Yes, for Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime (99.9% typical) and can include specific credits in the contract. Hosted has published uptime but enterprise SLA is negotiable on Dedicated commitments.
[09:03] Marta Gomez: A few CAIQ-specific asks: network segmentation diagrams and egress control configs. Can you provide a standard network diagram for Hosted and Dedicated?
[09:12] Ava Chen: Yes	6 we'll include a network diagram for Hosted and a separate one for Dedicated/Private (VPC peering, private endpoints, no public internet for data plane).
[09:27] Dinah Park: For Private deployments, what's the installation model? Air-gapped on prem or customer-managed cloud?

[09:34] Riley Patel: We offer a private control plane with customer-managed networking. On-prem air-gapped installs are possible with our on-prem package; we'll include the checklist for air-gapped requirements.
[09:51] Jordan Lee: Heading into questions about personnel security	6 background checks and least privilege for ops	6 Riley, you want to cover that?

[09:56] Riley Patel: Sure. Ops staff undergo background checks per our HR policy; privileged access is gated by RBAC and approval workflows, with MFA enforced. We'll include HR policy excerpts and an access review cadence.
[10:12] Marta Gomez: Do you provide proof of SOC 2 controls like evidence of access reviews?
[10:17] Riley Patel: We can provide a sample access review report and the process description; redacted to remove customer-identifying info.
[10:26] Ava Chen: Note for evidence: some customers request console screenshots plus API logs to show the same change. We'll include both where feasible.
[10:36] Liam O'Connor: Any encryption of backups? Are backups also in-region?

[10:41] Ava Chen: Backups are encrypted with the same at-rest encryption; for Hosted backups in EU are stored in EU by default when the tenant is EU-region. We'll include the backup retention and geo-location details.
[10:54] Marta Gomez: On data deletion / right to be forgotten	6 what is the deletion process and timeline?

[11:00] Riley Patel: We support data deletion requests; for Hosted customers deletion of customer data is typically within 30 days, with metadata cleanup processes documented. For Dedicated/Private it's under customer control.
[11:16] Jordan Lee: We're about 10 minutes in	6 quick pivot to evidence logistics: how do you want to receive the files? Secure FTP, encrypted email, or a shared secure bucket?
[11:27] Marta Gomez: Prefer secure S3 bucket or a secure transfer with a signed URL. Avoid email attachments for reports with sensitive details.
[11:35] Jordan Lee: We'll stage materials in a secure S3 with pre-signed URLs. I will share access with Verdant's vendor risk team only.
[11:42] Dinah Park: A couple of SIEM questions: can we get event timestamps in UTC and a mapping of event schema?
[11:48] Ava Chen: Yes, audit exports use UTC timestamps. We'll provide an event schema mapping doc in the evidence pack.
[11:58] Marta Gomez: Onchange management	6 do you have a schedule of planned maintenance and notifications?

[12:05] Riley Patel: Maintenance windows are published and we notify customers via email and console banners. Emergency changes follow our change control process; we'll include the changelog and release governance docs.
[12:19] Liam O'Connor: For downstream model data	6 does Redwood ever use customer prompts for model training or improvement?

[12:26] Jordan Lee: By default, we don't use customer data to train public models. We offer a separate opt-in program; policy and data handling are in the DPA. We'll attach the DPA excerpt clarifying data usage.
[12:40] Marta Gomez: Good. For the SIG Qs around multi-tenancy isolation, can you speak to how compute isolation is enforced?

[12:47] Ava Chen: Compute isolation for Hosted uses container and GPU tenancy isolation. Dedicated customers get reserved GPU pools; Private gets customer-managed instances. We'll include a short whitepaper on isolation strategies.
[13:03] Dinah Park: Anything on supply chain / dependencies? We need to know about third-party subprocessors and subvendors.
[13:09] Riley Patel: We maintain a subprocessors list and have contractual flow-downs for security controls. We'll provide a current list and our vendor management policy.
[13:22] Jordan Lee: Let's surface the highest-priority SIG items Verdant will need evidence for	6 Marta, can you call those out?
[13:29] Marta Gomez: Top ones: SOC 2 report, pen test summary, KMS architecture and BYOK evidence, RBAC screenshots + audit export, network diagram for EU hosting, and incident response policy.
[13:43] Jordan Lee: Great. We'll map those to owners and provide the artifacts. Expect initial bundle by 2026-03-30 and supplementary items the following week.

[13:51] Ava Chen: Quick technical note	6 when we export RBAC events the field names are sometimes different between internal logs and the UI labels; we'll annotate that to avoid confusion in your SIG responses.
[14:05] Marta Gomez: One more: do you have coverage for privacy impact assessments or DPIAs if we need them?
[14:11] Riley Patel: We can provide a DPIA template and examples of completed assessments for similar European customers; full DPIA with legal input typically requires more time.
[14:25] Liam O'Connor: For the follow-up tech deep dive, we'd like Dinah and two infra engineers to attend and test a small demo of SAML provisioning and log export. Week of 2026-04-06 works.
[14:35] Jordan Lee: Noted. I'll propose slots after the evidence pack goes out. Anything else from Verdant?
[14:41] Marta Gomez: No, that covers the bulk. Appreciate the transparency. We'll expect the SOC 2 and architecture diagram first.

[14:49] Jordan Lee: Thanks all	6 quick recap: Jordan to send SOC 2 and compliance pack 3/30, Ava to send architecture + RBAC screenshots 3/31, Riley will pull pen test and IR excerpts 4/2. Verdant to return prioritized SIG by 4/6 and we'll schedule the tech deep dive week of 4/6. I'll follow up with a calendar invite and secure S3 link.
[15:12] Marta Gomez: Thanks, we'll review and come back with any clarifying questions.
[15:18] Liam O'Connor: Thanks everyone, bye.
[15:20] Jordan Lee: Thanks, bye.
